title: Local SEO & Google Business Profile for Car Dealerships
description: Get your dealership into the Google local pack for the searches that end in a visit. Profile build-out, weekly posts and photos, review replies and local pages.
h1: Show up when someone nearby is ready to buy.
intro: When a shopper searches your brand plus your city, or "used trucks near me", Google shows three stores in the map pack. Those three get most of the calls and direction requests. This service is about being one of them — and looking like the obvious choice when you are.
signs: You don't show in the map pack for your own brand plus your city
Your Google profile has old photos, no recent posts, or the wrong hours
Service and parts calls go to reception because there's one phone number
A competitor with fewer reviews outranks you
Nobody at the store owns the profile week to week
steps: Fix the foundation
Primary and secondary categories, name, departments, hours, phone numbers, website link with tracking, description and attributes. Most stores gain ground from this step alone.
Build the weekly habit
One real post, five new photos and replies to every new review, every week. I do it, or I set it up so your team can keep it going.
Add the pages that back it up
Location and model-line pages on your website that match what people search, so Google and AI assistants have something solid to point to.
Track what matters
Calls, direction requests and website clicks from the profile, plus your position in the map pack for the searches that matter — by model line, not vanity keywords.
measure: Map pack position for your top 10 searches
faqs: How long does local SEO take to work for a dealership?
Profile fixes can move things in a few weeks. Steady gains in the map pack usually take two to four months of consistent posting, photos and reviews. Anyone promising page one in a week is guessing.
Do I need a separate profile for service and parts?

Usually one profile with departments set up properly is best — separate hours and phone numbers for sales, service and parts. Some larger stores also have separate listings that Google allows. I'll look at your setup and tell you which fits.
Can you guarantee a top-3 spot in the map pack?

No, and you should be wary of anyone who does. Distance from the searcher matters a lot and nobody controls that. What I can do is fix everything that is in your control, and show you the numbers every month.

title: Social Media Marketing for Car Dealerships
description: Dealership social that looks like your store, not a template. A monthly content plan, real photos and short video from your lot, and comment and message handling.
h1: Social that looks like your store, not a stock photo library.
intro: Shoppers check your Facebook and Instagram before they visit, even if they never message you. A page full of manufacturer graphics and posts from last spring tells them nobody is home. Real people, real cars and a steady rhythm tell them the opposite.
signs: Posts happen when someone remembers
Most of what you post is stock or manufacturer creative
Messages and comments sit unanswered for days
Video gets talked about but never happens
You can't say whether social has sold a single car
steps: Set a simple monthly plan
A calendar built around what your team can actually shoot: fresh trades, deliveries, team, service tips and community. Twelve post types, repeated.
Shoot it on the lot
Phone photos and short vertical video from your store, with clear rules on what needs a manager's OK and what doesn't.
Write it like a person
Captions in your store's voice — short, local and useful. No "elevate your driving experience".
Answer people
Comments and messages handled quickly, with leads passed to the right person and logged in the CRM.
faqs: Which social platforms should a dealership be on?
Facebook and Instagram first for most stores in Canada and the US. Add TikTok or YouTube Shorts if someone on your team enjoys making video — consistency matters more than the platform.
How often should a car dealership post?
Three to five times a week is plenty if the posts are real. One honest post beats five recycled ones.
Do you run social ads too?
Yes, as part of the paid side or the full retainer. Organic posting and ads work better together because the ads can use what already performs.

title: Email Marketing for Car Dealerships
description: Turn your customer database into appointments: equity mining, service-to-sales, lease maturity and sold-customer follow-up, measured on bookings.
h1: Your database is the cheapest inventory of buyers you own.
intro: Every customer who bought or serviced with you is already in your system. Most stores send them one blast a month — or nothing. A few well-aimed emails to the right people book more appointments than a lot of paid leads, at a fraction of the cost.
signs: One monthly newsletter goes to everyone
Equity and lease-maturity customers aren't contacted on purpose
Service customers never hear from sales
Nobody knows which emails booked an appointment
Your list hasn't been cleaned in years
steps: Segment what you have
Split the database by equity position, last service visit, lease or finance term, and last contact. Five useful lists beat one big one.
Write campaigns that sound human
Short, specific emails from a real person at the store, with one clear next step: book, reply or view a vehicle.
Build the always-on sequences
Service-to-sales, lease maturity, sold-customer follow-up and win-back — set up once, running every month.
Measure on appointments
Track replies, bookings and sold units from each campaign, not open rates.
faqs: Is dealership email marketing allowed under CASL?

Yes, with consent and proper unsubscribe handling. Canada's anti-spam law has specific rules on implied and express consent. I set campaigns up to respect them, and I'll flag anything your current setup is missing — but check with your compliance person too.
Which email platform do you use?
Usually the one your CRM already includes. Moving platforms is rarely the fix — better lists and better emails are.
How often should we email customers?
Two to four targeted emails a month across segments is typical. Each person should only get what's relevant to them.

title: Reputation Management for Car Dealerships
description: More honest 5-star reviews from sales and service, calm replies to the bad ones, and a Google rating that reflects how your store treats people.
h1: A rating that matches how you actually treat people.
intro: Shoppers read your reviews before they read your website. AI assistants summarize them when someone asks which store to trust. One angry review at the top of your profile can cost more than any ad you're running — and the fix is a process, not a campaign.
signs: Your rating is lower than your CSI scores suggest
Reviews come in bursts, then nothing for weeks
Bad reviews sit unanswered, or get defensive replies
Service gets fewer reviews than sales
Nobody knows whose job reviews are
steps: Build the ask into the process
A review request at every delivery and every service visit, by text with a direct link — timed for when the customer is happiest.
Reply to everything
Short, specific, human replies to every review. Calm, factual replies to the unfair ones, with a named manager to call.
Spot the patterns
Monthly read of what reviews actually say, so the store can fix the issue behind the complaints — not just answer them.
Report the trend
Rating, volume, recency and reply rate, by department, every month.
measure: New reviews per month, sales and service
faqs: Can you remove bad Google reviews?
Only reviews that break Google's policies can be removed, like spam or conflicts of interest. I'll flag those. For everything else, a good reply and a steady flow of new reviews is the real fix.
Is it OK to ask customers for reviews?
Yes. Asking every customer is fine and encouraged. What's not allowed is offering incentives or only asking happy customers through a filter. I keep the process within Google's rules.
How many reviews does a dealership need?
Recency matters as much as total count. A steady flow every week beats a big total that stopped growing last year. The review calculator shows what it takes to move your rating.
